liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (1 review): Reviewer notes a Sugaree lasting about sixteen minutes [24]
- **On The Road Again** (1 review): Electric version is rare, but the taper's mic handling spoils the recording of it [24]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Reviewer hears tight, intense 1982 jamming at the end of China before the transition [20]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Weir scats along note for note with Jerry; reviewer knows of no other time [24]
- **Playing In The Band Jam** (1 review): Bobby scats over the start of the Playin' jam, which reviewer had never heard before [25]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-07-27.sbd.clemens.78746.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 131 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1982-07-27.mtx.sirmick.109780.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 135 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard supplies crisp vocals the audience tape lacks; the audience tape has better high end [2]
- **gd1982-07-27.167100.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.sclugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 137 min [4]
- **gd1982-07-27.156435.beyer.m88.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 135 min [6]
- **gd82-07-27.fob-senn421.wise.4705.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 135 min; rated 4.4/5 by 20 [15]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds Red Rocks audience tapes beat soundboards, with brighter Jerry, fuller Phil and more forward band; Microphones sound placed directly in front of Garcia; Decent but unremarkable audience recording with Jerry loudest; rain may have meant plastic covering the mics [22][23][25]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended all three Red Rocks nights in rain; this night was only misty and drizzly [18]
- John Coit of the Rocky Mountain News, a friendly Dead chronicler, wrote about the 27th [18]
- It rained all three nights, yet the band stayed at Red Rocks instead of moving to Boulder [26]
- The following night, the 28th, was wetter, when a tropical monsoon rolled in [18]
- Reviewer finds this show matches the energetic, daring jamming of other summer 1982 tour recordings [23]
- Weir did similar scatting on 12/27/81, with less screaming and a smoother result [27]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-07-27.sbd.clemens.78746.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Jake Clemens; source: SBD>Cass/1>DAT [1]
- **gd1982-07-27.mtx.sirmick.109780.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SIRMick; source: Matrix 60% soundboard/40% audience; sources: 1 - SBD>Cass/1>DAT>HD-P2>Soundforge 6.0>Flac Frontend>FLAC (shnid 78746) Tranfer by Jake Clemens 2 - (FOB)… [2]. Also: Matrix blend of a soundboard and an audience recording, made by combining the two sources [2]
- **gd1982-07-27.167100.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.sclugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [4]. Also: A Beyer M160 and Sennheiser 421 blend source patches 13 seconds in The Wheel space [4]
- **gd1982-07-27.156435.beyer.m88.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Beyer M88 mics > Unknown deck > Jim Vita's 1st generation cassettes (Maxell MX-90) [6]. Also: Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies On The Road Again, most of Roses, and Rider's final 4:14; Doug Lamarre's Nakamichi 300 source fills a 47-second patch in Drums [6]
- **gd82-07-27.fob-senn421.wise.4705.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [15]

Matrix blend of a soundboard and an audience recording, made by combining the two sources
Soundboard supplies crisp vocals the audience tape lacks; the audience tape has better high end
Source cassettes and transfer by Scott Wiseman; Charlie Miller coordinated the project
A Beyer M160 and Sennheiser 421 blend source patches 13 seconds in The Wheel space
First-generation cassettes from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller, who coordinated the effort
Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies On The Road Again, most of Roses, and Rider's final 4:14
Doug Lamarre's Nakamichi 300 source fills a 47-second patch in Drums
